title: Showdown - BYOB*
author: Emotional-Breath-838
selftext:
I’m looking for a competitive platform that allows entrants to bring their own AI bots and their own trading strategies to compete. 

Three arenas…

Day trade - purely agentic for five trading days 

Swing trade - human assisted for two weeks 

Investor - human assisted over a month 

Bragging rights or prizes.    
Sponsored or not.     
All AI models are allowed. 

Does this exist? 

If not, why not? 

\*bring your own bot

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: closest things i know of are Quantiacs and Numerai, and neither is quite it. Quantiacs runs your code on their data with their simulator, Numerai only takes signals. nothing agentic-for-five-days exists that i have seen. the why is the simulator. if every entrant brings their own data feed and their own assumption about what price they got, the winner is whoever assumed the kindest prices, so a fair contest has to run every bot through one engine, and that is a lot of work for bragging rights. I built Quantradin, which does the one-engine half of that, every strategy gets the same prices and the same grade, it only ever trades paper money and costs nothing, but it is a desk, not a contest.

replies.author: Emotional-Breath-838
replies.body:
Ah.  The data feed and fills would have to be standardized.  

So, it sounds like it can’t be done unless you have a broker host the contest.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: not a broker exactly, a simulator. the host needs one price feed and one fill model that every bot goes through. a broker is one way to get that, but any shared engine does it. the hard part is people trusting the host's fills over their own.

comments.author: SuperOrbital_Trading
comments.body: You could easily make something like this via reddit/discord. Honestly, any of the companies that let you use your own bot are just using you to compile data to improve their own models and ultimately take more from retail. I tend to avoid them.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body:
It exists in pieces, but nothing covers all three arenas with bring-your-own-bot. Alpha Arena-style model showdowns and paper-trading leagues cover parts of it, but most are fixed-model or single-format.

The main reason it's hard is fairness and verification. Entrants need identical data and timestamps, or you're mostly ranking who has the better feed. You also need pre-committed, frozen predictions so nobody can edit history, and a way to tell "purely agentic" from "human-assisted" in the day-trade arena. A one-week window is also mostly noise, so a good format would score risk-adjusted returns across several rounds, not raw P&L.

Something like EventTrader, which we build at Cymetica, could serve as the common event layer: structured, timestamped earnings and macro data every bot reads from. That levels the input side, so the competition tests reasoning, not data plumbing.  [https://claude.ai/artifact/VuwYE2KYrtzMdwyEpvA9wH](https://claude.ai/artifact/VuwYE2KYrtzMdwyEpvA9wH)

replies.author: Emotional-Breath-838
replies.body: I would love to see which traders and bots and AI models could win a fair fight in a level field arena.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body:
Same, I'd watch that closely. The part that would make it credible is publishing everything in the open: the rules, the frozen entries before each round, and the results, including the rounds where the favorites lose. Three or four rounds with different regimes would also tell you more than one big final, since one strong week usually just rewards whoever took the most risk.

Adding a plain buy-and-hold or equal-weight entry as a baseline would be a nice touch as well. If a lot of the fancy bots can't beat it after costs, that's worth knowing too. Which arena do you think would be the hardest to keep fair, the day-trade one?
